note: Governs how an AI generator may consume tokens/llm/token-catalog.json. Category keys under rawValueRestrictions match token-catalog.json's own top-level foundation subkeys exactly (color, typography, radius, breakpoint, elevation, icon-size, motion) so a drift check can resolve every key against something real -- per MASTER-GUIDE.md 3.21's warning against inventing convenient-but-unresolvable category names.

semanticPreference.rule: A generator must reference a semantic token (text.*, surface.*, border.*, accent.*) over a foundation token (color.*) wherever a semantic id exists for the intended use. Foundation color.* ids exist to define the available palette, not to be referenced directly by a generated PageSpec or a new section contract.
semanticPreference.rationale: Foundation defines available values; semantic tokens define intent (per this workspace's Genesis principle -- reference color.surface.brand, never #262521, at the point of use). Only semantic.json and component.json are permitted to reference tokens/00-foundation/*.json aliases directly.
semanticPreference.exception: typography.*, radius.*, breakpoint.*, elevation.*, icon-size.*, and motion.* have no semantic layer in this design-repo (10-semantic/semantic.json only defines color-derived roles) -- these foundation categories may be referenced directly by section/primitive/component contracts. This is a real, checked absence, not an oversight: grep of tokens/10-semantic/semantic.json confirms it defines only text/surface/border/accent.

rawValueRestrictions.rule: A generator must never emit a raw literal value (a hex/rgba color, a px/em size, a cubic-bezier array, a spring/tween object) where a matching token id exists in token-catalog.json. A raw value is permitted ONLY when no catalog id covers that exact value -- and even then, the correct fix is usually to add the missing token to the real foundation file first, not to hardcode it into a generated instance.
rawValueRestrictions.enforcementScope: This restriction governs section/component/primitive contracts and any future generator output that carries a style/token field. It does NOT govern schema/pagespec.schema.json's existing node.content or node.motion fields directly, because -- confirmed by direct inspection of schema/pagespec.schema.json and schema/example.pagespec.json -- no PageSpec node carries a per-instance style/token-override field at all; content fields are copy (headings, body text, hrefs) and motion fields are a closed pattern/reducedMotionFallback enum, never a raw style value. See the 'overrides' section below for what this means for PageSpec-level enforcement.

categories.color: No raw hex/rgb/rgba color value in a new contract where tokens/00-foundation/color.json (directly) or tokens/10-semantic/semantic.json (preferred, per semanticPreference above) already defines that value.
categories.typography: No raw font-size/line-height/letter-spacing triple where tokens/00-foundation/typography.json#/typeScale already defines an equivalent named scale step.
categories.radius: No raw border-radius px value where tokens/00-foundation/radius.json#/radii already defines it.
categories.breakpoint: No raw px breakpoint literal where tokens/00-foundation/breakpoint.json#/breakpoints already defines it.
categories.elevation: No raw box-shadow string where tokens/00-foundation/elevation.json#/shadows already defines it.
categories.icon-size: No raw icon dimension where tokens/00-foundation/icon-size.json#/sizes already defines it.
categories.motion: No raw cubic-bezier array, spring config, or tween config where tokens/00-foundation/motion.json already defines an equivalent named easing/spring/tween. A PageSpec node's motion.pattern field (a free-form string, e.g. 'fade-in') is not itself a raw motion value in this sense -- it names a pattern, it does not encode timing -- so it is exempt from this restriction; only a literal duration/easing/bounce/stiffness value would violate it.

overrides.rule: A permitted local override exists only at the component-token layer (tokens/20-component/component.json), which is explicitly allowed to restate a foundation/semantic value in a component-scoped shape (e.g. button.primary.light.hover.bg) -- this is the one legitimate 'override' point in this design-repo's resolution chain, not a general per-instance escape hatch.
overrides.pageSpecLevelOverrideGap: This design-repo's schema/pagespec.schema.json carries no per-instance token-override field on any node (confirmed by direct inspection, per MASTER-GUIDE.md 3.21) -- a generated PageSpec cannot override a token's value at all, permitted or otherwise, because there is no field through which to do so. If a future revision of pagespec.schema.json adds such a field, this policy's overrides rule must be extended to state which token categories that field may touch and which remain closed, and a matching adversarial PageSpec-mutation case must be added to schema/tests/adversarial_test.py at that time. Until then, override enforcement lives entirely at the catalog/policy layer (see extraction/verify_all.py's token-catalog and token-policy checks), not the PageSpec layer.
overrides.responsiveOverrides: tokens/30-layout/layout.json#/sectionPadding and #/grid already encode the only permitted per-breakpoint value variation (phone/tablet/desktop) in this design-repo; a generator may select among these three breakpoint keys but must not invent a fourth breakpoint or a value outside this file.

resolutionOrder: foundation (tokens/00-foundation/**) -- the closed set of available raw values
theme-mode overrides (tokens/themes/light.json#/resolves) -- resolves a subset of semantic ids to a concrete foundation value for a given theme

semantic aliases (tokens/10-semantic/semantic.json) -- intent-named roles, each pointing at a foundation id via {color.x} alias syntax or, for the ids the theme file covers, resolved per the active theme
component tokens (tokens/20-component/component.json) -- component-scoped restatement/composition of semantic+foundation values for a specific interactive state (rest/hover/idle/success/error)
layout tokens (tokens/30-layout/layout.json) -- grid/spacing/max-width values, independent of the color resolution chain above
permitted local overrides -- none beyond the component-token layer itself; see overrides.pageSpecLevelOverrideGap
responsive overrides -- tokens/30-layout/layout.json's own phone/tablet/desktop keys only
inheritance.rule: Never resolve a semantic alias before the active theme is known -- tokens/10-semantic/semantic.json's '{color.x}' aliases are foundation-direct (theme-independent, since this design-repo has exactly one theme instance), but text.primary/text.inverse/surface.page/surface.brand/surface.subtle/surface.card/border.default are additionally listed in tokens/themes/light.json#/resolves and must be read through the active theme (registry.manifest.json's defaultTheme, currently 'light') rather than assumed constant, in case a second theme instance is ever added.
inheritance.singleThemeNote: tokens/themes/light.json's own note field states this design-repo is single-theme (no dark-mode toggle observed in src/); this inheritance order is written to remain correct if a second theme is added later, not because multiple themes exist today.

themeResolutionBehavior.activeTheme: Read from registry.manifest.json#/defaultTheme (currently 'light'); a generator must never hardcode 'light' -- it must read the active theme id from the manifest so this policy keeps working if defaultTheme changes.
resolutionSteps: 1. Look up the semantic id in tokens/themes/<activeTheme>.json#/resolves.
2. If present, use that theme-resolved value (already a concrete foundation value, per tokens/themes/light.json's own construction).

3. If absent from the theme file (true today for text.muted, text.faqAnswer, border.focus, surface.paper, and all accent.* ids), resolve the semantic id's own foundation alias directly from tokens/10-semantic/semantic.json instead -- these ids are theme-independent by construction in this design-repo, not a gap in the theme file.

4. Never fall back to a raw literal at this step; if neither the theme file nor semantic.json resolves the id, the id does not exist in this catalog and must be rejected (see extraction/verify_all.py's token-catalog check and the adversarial 'unknown token id' case).
